content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I've drafted the baseline specification. Per our Spec-Driven Development workflow, **this is the first gate — please review the spec before we plan or build anything.**

## 📋 Specification ready for your review

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: all 16 items pass; no open clarifications

### What the spec proposes

**Core loop (MVP, P1)**
- **Save a bookmark** — paste a web address, optional custom title; auto-labels from the page title or the address itself
- **Browse & open** — see all saved bookmarks in a list, click to open the original page in a new tab

**Managing (P2)**
- **Edit & delete** — fix a title/address, or remove with a confirmation step

**Organizing (P3)**
- **Tags & search** — tag bookmarks, filter by tag, and keyword-search across title/address/tags

**Also covered**: validation of malformed addresses, duplicate-address warnings, empty/no-results states, best-effort page-title fetching, and most-recent-first ordering.

### Scope boundaries I assumed (please confirm or correct)

| Assumption | In v1? |
|---|---|
| Single local user — no accounts/login | ✅ in / others out |
| Web pages (HTTP/HTTPS) only | ✅ in |
| Local persistence (survives reload) | ✅ in |
| Cross-device sync / cloud backup | ❌ out |
| Import/export of existing browser bookmarks | ❌ out |
| Dedicated mobile layout | ❌ out (later) |

### A few questions worth settling now (optional — happy to proceed as-is)

1. **Tags & search (P3)** — keep in scope, or trim v1 to just save/browse/edit/delete?
2. **Auto page-title fetching** — worth the complexity, or start with manual titles only?
3. **Anything missing** — e.g. favicons, notes/descriptions, favorites/pinning, folders?

---

**How would you like to proceed?**
- ✅ **Approve as-is** → I'll move to the plan gate (`speckit-plan`)
- ✏️ **Request changes** → I'll revise the spec (`speckit-specify`) before planning

I'll hold here and won't start planning or coding until you approve.
Approve as-is. Please keep tags, search, and best-effort page-title fetching in v1, then move on to the planning stage.

No `after_plan` hooks. Phase 1 design is complete. Per our workflow, **this is the plan gate — please review before we break it into tasks or build.**

## 🛠️ Implementation Plan ready for review

- **Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`
- **Artifacts**: `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `quickstart.md`
- **Constitution check**: PASS (constitution is an unpopulated template — no gates to enforce; plan follows simplicity/testability defaults)

### The approach in plain terms

**One small web app, no external services.** A single Node.js server both serves the web page and answers data requests, and bookmarks are stored in a local database file so they survive restarts.

| Area | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Stack** | Node.js + Express, plain HTML/CSS/JS front-end | No build step; simple and inspectable |
| **Storage** | SQLite file under `data/` | Survives reloads (SC-002); no server to run; real queries for tags/search |
| **Addresses** | Standard URL parser, `http`/`https` only, normalized | Rejects bad links (SC-004); reliable duplicate detection (FR-009) |
| **Page titles** | Fetched best-effort on save (~5s cap), falls back to the address | Never blocks or fails a save (FR-003) |
| **Search & tags** | Handled server-side | Finds one of 100 in seconds (SC-003) |
| **Testing** | `node:test` (unit) + Playwright 1.61.0 (end-to-end) | Covers the acceptance scenarios |

### How it maps to your app

- **API**: list/create/edit/delete bookmarks, list tags — with keyword search (`q`) and tag filtering built into the list endpoint (see `contracts/api.md`).
- **UI**: a bookmark list with an add form, inline edit, delete-with-confirmation, tag filter chips, and a search box — plus distinct "empty" vs "no results" states.
- **Data**: `Bookmark` (url, title, timestamps) ↔ `Tag` many-to-many.

### Notable decisions to confirm

1. **Vanilla front-end** (no React/framework) to keep v1 lightweight — good, or would you prefer a framework?
2. **SQLite file** for storage (single-user, local) — fits the "no external service" environment; acceptable?
3. **Plain substring search** (not full-text indexing) — sufficient at v1 scale; fine to start here?

---

**How would you like to proceed?**
- ✅ **Approve the plan** → I'll generate the task breakdown (`speckit-tasks`), then, on your go-ahead, implement.
- ✏️ **Request changes** → I'll revise the plan before moving on.

All 31 tasks are complete and marked `[X]`. No `after_implement` hooks are registered. Implementation is finished and verified.

## ✅ Implementation complete — Bookmark Manager v1

**Tests: 24/24 unit passing · 11/11 end-to-end passing.** The app was smoke-tested against the production `npm start` command and binds `0.0.0.0:4000`.

### What was built

A single Node.js + Express app serving a JSON API and a vanilla-JS frontend, with SQLite persistence — exactly the approved plan.

| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| **Server** | `server/index.js`, `server/app.js`, `server/db.js`, `server/bookmarks.repo.js`, `server/routes/{bookmarks,tags}.js` |
| **Shared libs** | `server/lib/url.js` (validate/normalize), `server/lib/title.js` (best-effort title fetch) |
| **Frontend** | `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `public/styles.css` |
| **Tests** | `tests/unit/*.test.js` (3 files), `tests/e2e/*.spec.js` (4 files) |
| **Config** | `package.json`, `playwright.config.js`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `.harness/app.json` |

### All four user stories delivered
- **US1 Save** — validate URL (http/https only), best-effort page-title fetch with fallback, duplicate rejection, persisted with timestamps.
- **US2 Browse/open** — newest-first list, titles open in a new tab, distinct empty state.
- **US3 Edit/delete** — inline edit, delete-with-confirmation, changes persist.
- **US4 Tags/search** — tag filter chips, keyword search across title/address/tags, distinct no-results state.

### Two implementation notes (fidelity to spec/plan, no behavior change)
1. **Test script uses a glob** (`node --test "tests/unit/**/*.test.js"`) rather than the literal `node --test tests/unit` in the task text — Node 24's runner treats a bare directory as a file. Same intent, working command.
2. **Added a test-only reset endpoint** (`POST /api/test/reset`) gated behind `ENABLE_TEST_RESET=1`, set only by the Playwright runner — never enabled in the delivered app. This gives the E2E suite clean isolation.

Neither touches the spec's behavior; both are within the plan's testing approach, so no spec/plan revision is warranted.

### Ready for review
Port 4000 was left free, so the harness will start a **fresh, empty** instance (the empty state is a valid ready state and is marked `data-harness-ready="true"`). The client reaches it at **`http://maker:4000`**.

**Try:** add a URL (e.g. `https://example.com`) → see it listed → tag it, search/filter it → edit or delete it.

If anything looks off during your review, tell me and I'll route it correctly — a divergence from the approved spec I'll fix by continuing implementation; a genuine spec change I'll take back through `speckit-specify` and re-plan before rebuilding, per our SDD workflow.
The completed app matches the behavior we approved, and the verification results cover all four user stories. I accept Bookmark Manager v1.
